records.source: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;
records.gloss: Said then the high priest, If these things so are?
pieces: The high priest asked, "Are these charges true?"

L.1: Then the high priest said, "Are these things so?"

R.1: Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Is this true?"

decisions.choice: the high priest: the head of the council before which Stephen stands
decisions.reason: The high priest led the council (5:21, 5:27). Acts does not name him here; Annas and Caiaphas are named among the high priestly family in 4:6.

decisions.choice: are these things so: a direct question whether the charges are true
alternatives: if these things are so (a condition)
decisions.reason: The small word that usually means "if" can introduce a direct question (1:6). "These things" are the charges of 6:13-14, that Stephen spoke against the temple and the law.

decisions.choice: these charges; Stephen
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "these things" are, and Readable names the one asked, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: Stephen answers the council

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.
records.gloss: He then said, Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of the glory appeared to the father of us Abraham being in the Mesopotamia before rather dwelling him in Haran, \v 3 and said to him, Go out from the land of you and from the kindred of you, and come into the land which ever to you I will show.
pieces: Stephen replied, "Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
God said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your kin, and come to the land that I will show you.'

L.2: And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
L.3: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.'

R.2: Stephen answered, "Brothers and leaders of our people, listen to me. Long ago the God of glory came and showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Abraham, the father of our nation. At that time Abraham lived in Mesopotamia. He had not yet moved to Haran.
R.3: God said to him, 'Leave your country and your relatives. Go to the land that I will show you.'

decisions.choice: men, brothers and fathers: a formal address to the council, honoring its older members as fathers
alternatives: an address to men and women
decisions.reason: Stephen speaks to the council (6:12, 6:15), whose members were all men, so the address is not widened to men and women, as with Gamaliel's address to the council (5:35). "Fathers" honors the elders and leaders among them; Paul opens his speech to a Jerusalem crowd with "brothers and fathers" (22:1).

decisions.choice: the God of glory: God who shows himself in his glory
alternatives: the glorious God, without the sense of appearing
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Psalm 29:3. The God who "appeared" is the God whose glory is seen, and the speech ends with Stephen seeing the glory of God (7:55).

decisions.choice: Abraham was called while in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran
alternatives: the call came in Haran, as the order of Genesis 11:31-12:4 might suggest
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:31 tells how Terah took Abram from Ur of the Chaldeans to Haran, and the call of Genesis 12:1 is told after that, with Abram leaving Haran (12:4). Stephen places God's appearing before Haran, in Mesopotamia, which 7:4 calls the land of the Chaldeans. Genesis 15:7 and Nehemiah 9:7 say that God brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and Joshua 24:2-3 that God took him from beyond the river. Genesis does not report a call in Ur in so many words. The text is translated as it stands, without settling how the two accounts fit together.

decisions.choice: God's words are Genesis 12:1
alternatives: a summary in Stephen's own words
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 12:1 closely, but leave out "and from your father's house".

decisions.choice: Brothers and fathers
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the formal opening word "men", which English does not use in this kind of address; Literal keeps it. No gender setting applies, since the hearers were all men.

decisions.choice: leaders of our people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom "fathers" honors here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: came and showed himself; the father of our nation
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "appeared" means and in what sense Abraham is "our father".

records.source: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν.
records.gloss: Then having gone out from [the] land of Chaldeans he dwelt in Haran.
pieces: So he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran.

L.4: Then, going out from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, he lived in Haran.

R.4: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and went to live in Haran.

decisions.choice: the land of the Chaldeans: southern Mesopotamia, the region of Ur
decisions.reason: Genesis calls Abram's first home "Ur of the Chaldeans" (Genesis 11:28, 11:31). Haran lay far to the northwest, on the way to Canaan.

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject.

records.source: κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.
records.gloss: And from there after the to die the father of him He removed him into the land this in which you now dwell, \v 5 and not He gave to him an inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and He promised to give to him for a possession it and to the seed of him after him, not being to him a child.
pieces: After his father's death, God moved him from there into this land where you now live.

He gave him no share of it to inherit, not even ground enough for one step. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him and to his descendants after him to hold as their own, while Abraham was still childless.

L.4: And from there, after his father died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved him into this land in which you now live.
L.5: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him no inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his seed after him, while he had no child.

R.4: After Abraham's father died, God brought Abraham to this land where you live now.
R.5: God did not give him any of the land to own, not even a small piece. But God promised that one day the land would belong to Abraham and to his family after him. God promised this even though Abraham did not have any children yet.

decisions.choice: Abraham left Haran after his father died
alternatives: Abraham left while his father was still alive
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:26 says Terah was seventy when he fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran; 11:32 says he died in Haran at 205; 12:4 says Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran. Taken together, and if Abram was the firstborn, these would have Terah still alive when Abram left. Genesis tells of Terah's death (11:32) before Abram's leaving (12:4), and Stephen follows that order. The Samaritan Pentateuch gives Terah's age at death in 11:32 as 145, which agrees with Stephen's order. Reviewers should check the Samaritan figure. The text does not explain more, and nothing is added to harmonize it.

decisions.choice: not even the step of a foot: not the smallest piece of ground
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 2:5 in the Greek Old Testament. Abraham later bought a field with a cave to bury Sarah (Genesis 23), but that was a purchase, not land given him to inherit.

decisions.choice: God's promise of the land to Abraham and his descendants
decisions.reason: Genesis 12:7, 13:15 and 17:8 promise the land to Abraham and his offspring; Genesis 17:8 and 48:4 call it a possession. The promise was made while Abraham had no son (Genesis 15:2-3).

decisions.choice: seed: descendants
decisions.reason: The singular word here means Abraham's offspring as a whole, as the next verse shows (7:6).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who moved Abraham; the Greek verb has no stated subject.

decisions.choice: God promised this even though
decisions.reason: Readable makes the closing phrase its own sentence.

records.source: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·
records.gloss: Spoke however thus the God, that will be the seed of him a sojourner in a land foreign, and they will enslave it and will mistreat years four hundred;
pieces: This is what God said: his descendants would live as outsiders in a land that belonged to others, and its people would make them slaves and treat them harshly for 400 years.

L.6: But God spoke in this way, that his seed would be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they would enslave it and mistreat [it] 400 years.

R.6: God also told Abraham that his family after him would live in a country that was not theirs. The people there would make them slaves and treat them badly for 400 years.

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:13, given as reported speech
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:13 closely. Stephen turns them into reported speech, then moves into God's own words in 7:7.

decisions.choice: four hundred years, the figure of Genesis 15:13
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:13 gives 400 years, and Stephen keeps that figure. Exodus 12:40-41 says Israel lived in Egypt 430 years; in the Greek Old Testament and the Samaritan Pentateuch that verse reads "in Egypt and in the land of Canaan". Paul counts 430 years from the promise to the law (Galatians 3:17). The speech quotes the figure of Genesis and does not say how the numbers relate.

decisions.choice: a sojourner: a foreigner living in a land without a citizen's rights
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Moses in Midian (7:29).

decisions.choice: God also told Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the one God spoke to.

decisions.choice: make them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.
records.gloss: And the nation to which ever they will serve as slaves will judge I, the God said, and after these things they will come out and will serve me in the place this.
pieces: 'But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves,' God said, 'and afterward they will come out and worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'

L.7: 'And the nation to which they will be slaves I will judge,' God said, 'and after these things they will come out and serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'

R.7: God said, 'But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. After that, they will leave that country, and they will worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} here in this place.'

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:14: God will judge the nation that enslaves them
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:14. The plagues on Egypt are that judgment (Exodus 6:6, 12:12).

decisions.choice: worship me in this place: the words of Exodus 3:12, with the place changed
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:14 ends with the people coming out with great possessions. The last words echo Exodus 3:12, where God tells Moses that the people will serve God "on this mountain". Here it is "this place". It may mean the land where Stephen's hearers live (7:4), or the temple, which the charges called "this place" (6:13-14). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: This verb is used of serving God in worship (Luke 2:37, 4:8); the same verb is used in 7:42 of worshiping the stars.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the word that shows this is worship; Literal keeps "serve".

decisions.choice: punish
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's judging the nation would mean for it.

decisions.choice: be slaves / serve as slaves / makes them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.
records.gloss: And he gave to him a covenant of circumcision; and thus he fathered the Isaac and circumcised him on the day the eighth, and Isaac the Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
pieces: God also gave him the covenant marked by circumcision. And so, when Isaac was born to Abraham, he circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac in turn had Jacob, and Jacob had the twelve patriarchs.

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him a covenant of circumcision. And so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac [fathered] Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

R.8: God made a covenant with Abraham, and circumcision was the mark of it. So when Abraham's son Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him when he was eight days old. Later Isaac had a son named Jacob. Jacob had twelve sons, and they were the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the covenant of circumcision: the covenant of Genesis 17, with circumcision as its mark
decisions.reason: In Genesis 17:9-14 God makes circumcision the sign of the covenant between him and Abraham's family.

decisions.choice: and so: under that covenant, Isaac was circumcised
alternatives: and in this way he became a father
decisions.reason: "So" ties Isaac's circumcision to the covenant just named. Genesis 21:4 says Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days old, as God had commanded.

decisions.choice: the twelve patriarchs: the twelve sons of Jacob, from whom the tribes of Israel came
decisions.reason: Genesis 35:22-26 and 49:28 list the twelve sons as the heads of the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver of the covenant.

decisions.choice: twelve sons, the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And the patriarchs having been jealous of the Joseph sold [him] into Egypt; and was the God with him \v 10 and rescued him out of all the afflictions of him and gave to him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruling over Egypt and all the house of him.
pieces: The patriarchs envied Joseph and sold him off to Egypt. Yet God stood by him
and delivered him from every hardship he met. He gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who made him governor over Egypt and over all his household.

L.9: And the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, sold [him] into Egypt. And God was with him,
L.10: and rescued him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his house.

R.9: Jacob's sons were jealous of their brother Joseph. They sold him, and he was taken to Egypt as a slave. But God was with Joseph.
R.10: God rescued him from all his troubles. God made him wise, and Pharaoh the king of Egypt was pleased with him. Pharaoh made Joseph the ruler over Egypt and over everyone in the king's household.

decisions.choice: the story of Joseph in Genesis 37-41
decisions.reason: His brothers were jealous of him (Genesis 37:11) and sold him (37:28); God was with him (39:2, 39:21); Pharaoh saw his wisdom and set him over Egypt and his house (41:37-44; see also 45:8).

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes
decisions.reason: The word is the one often translated grace, but here it means favor in the eyes of a person, as in Genesis 39:21, where God gave Joseph favor with the keeper of the prison.

decisions.choice: he appointed him: Pharaoh made Joseph ruler
decisions.reason: The subject changes from God to Pharaoh, as in Genesis 41:41-43.

decisions.choice: the brothers rejected the one God was with
alternatives: a story with no wider point
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers turn against him, yet God is with him and he becomes their rescuer. The speech shows the same pattern in Moses (7:25, 7:35) and comes at last to Jesus (7:52).

decisions.choice: Jacob's sons ... their brother Joseph ... as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were and that Joseph was sold as a slave (Genesis 37:28, 39:1).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... was pleased with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what favor before Pharaoh means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·
records.gloss: Came then a famine upon all the Egypt and Canaan and affliction great, and not were finding food the fathers of us.
pieces: Then famine struck the whole of Egypt and Canaan, bringing great hardship, and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could find nothing to eat.

L.11: Then a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers were not finding food.

R.11: Then there was a famine in all of Egypt and Canaan. People suffered terribly. Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could not find any food.

decisions.choice: the famine of Genesis 41-42
decisions.reason: Genesis 41:54-57 and 42:5 tell of the famine over Egypt and Canaan.

decisions.choice: food: provisions, anything to live on
decisions.reason: The word was first used of food for animals, but by this time it meant food in general.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here "fathers" means the whole household of Jacob, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·
records.gloss: Having heard then Jacob being grain into Egypt he sent out the fathers of us first;
pieces: When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our forefathers there on a first journey.

L.12: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers [the] first [time].

R.12: Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt. So he sent his sons, our forefathers, to buy some. This was their first trip.

decisions.choice: Genesis 42:1-3: Jacob sends his sons for grain
decisions.reason: Jacob sent ten of his sons and kept Benjamin at home (Genesis 42:3-4).

decisions.choice: our fathers: here the sons of Jacob
decisions.reason: The ones Jacob sent to Egypt were his sons, named men (Genesis 42:3), the forefathers of the tribes.

decisions.choice: our forefathers, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Here the word means particular men, the sons of Jacob, so the inclusive setting does not apply; "forefathers" says that plainly.

decisions.choice: his sons ... to buy some
decisions.reason: Readable names those sent and why they went (Genesis 42:2).

records.source: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος Ἰωσήφ.
records.gloss: and on the second was made known Joseph to the brothers of him, and known became to the Pharaoh the family of Joseph.
pieces: On their second visit Joseph let his brothers know who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.

L.13: And on the second [visit] Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh.

R.13: When they went to Egypt the second time, Joseph told his brothers who he was. And Pharaoh found out about Joseph's family.

decisions.choice: Genesis 45: Joseph makes himself known
decisions.reason: Joseph revealed himself to his brothers on their second journey (Genesis 45:1-4), and Pharaoh heard that Joseph's brothers had come (45:16).

decisions.choice: was made known: Joseph made himself known to them
decisions.reason: The passive verb can mean that Joseph let himself be known, as Genesis 45:1 says.

decisions.choice: their second visit
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "on the second"; Balanced and Readable supply the journey meant.

records.source: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε, καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
records.gloss: Having sent then Joseph called for Jacob the father of him and all the kindred in souls seventy-five; \v 15 and went down Jacob into Egypt.
pieces: Joseph sent for his father Jacob and for all his relatives, seventy-five people in all,
and Jacob went down to Egypt.

L.14: Then Joseph sent and summoned Jacob his father and all [his] relatives, seventy-five souls in all.
L.15: And Jacob went down into Egypt.

R.14: Joseph sent a message to his father Jacob. He asked him to come to Egypt with the whole family. There were seventy-five of them.
R.15: So Jacob went down to Egypt.

decisions.choice: seventy-five persons, the number in the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: seventy, the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text gives the number of Jacob's family who came to Egypt as seventy (Genesis 46:27; Exodus 1:5; Deuteronomy 10:22). The Greek Old Testament gives seventy-five in Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5, counting more of Joseph's descendants (Greek Genesis 46:20). A Hebrew manuscript of Exodus from Qumran also reads seventy-five in Exodus 1:5. Stephen gives the number found in the Greek. The counts also differ in whom they include: Genesis 46:26 gives sixty-six. Reviewers should check the Qumran reading.

decisions.choice: in souls: persons, people
decisions.reason: "Souls" here simply counts people, as in 2:41.

decisions.choice: Genesis 45:9-11 and 46:1-7
decisions.reason: Joseph sent for his father, and Jacob went down to Egypt with all his family.

decisions.choice: sent a message ... asked him to come to Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says what Joseph's sending meant.

records.source: καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ.
records.gloss: and died he and the fathers of us, \v 16 and they were carried over to Shechem and were placed in the tomb which bought Abraham for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
pieces: There he died, and so did our forefathers.
They were carried back to Shechem and laid in the tomb Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor at Shechem.

L.15: And he died, he and our fathers,
L.16: and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

R.15: Jacob died there. Our forefathers, his sons, died there too.
R.16: Later they were carried back to Shechem. They were buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem. He had paid for it with silver.

decisions.choice: the tomb at Shechem: Stephen's account, as it stands
alternatives: Stephen's account adjusted to agree with Genesis and Joshua
decisions.reason: Genesis 23 tells how Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah at Hebron from Ephron the Hittite, and Jacob was buried there (Genesis 49:29-32, 50:13). Jacob bought a piece of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor (Genesis 33:19), and Joseph's bones were buried there (Joshua 24:32). Abraham built an altar at Shechem (Genesis 12:6-7), but no purchase by him there is recorded. The Old Testament does not say where Joseph's brothers were buried. Stephen's words join Abraham's purchase with the place and sellers of Jacob's. The text gives no explanation, and this translation renders it as it stands.

decisions.choice: they were carried: our fathers, and perhaps Jacob with them
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It may take in Jacob as well as the fathers; Genesis 50:13 says Jacob was buried at Hebron. Literal and Balanced keep "they" open.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the sons of Hamor in Shechem"
alternatives: "the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "Hamor the father of Shechem", as in Genesis 33:19; others have "of Shechem". Several early manuscripts have "in Shechem". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: our forefathers, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: These are Jacob's sons, particular men, so the inclusive setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: his sons ... Later
decisions.reason: Readable says who the fathers were and that the burial came later.

records.source: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.
records.gloss: As now was drawing near the time of the promise which had declared the God to the Abraham, grew the people and multiplied in Egypt \v 18 until which arose king another over Egypt who not knew the Joseph.
pieces: The time was coming close for the promise God had pledged to Abraham, and the people grew and multiplied in Egypt
until another king rose to rule Egypt, a king who knew nothing of Joseph.

L.17: And as the time of the promise which God had declared to Abraham was drawing near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
L.18: until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

R.17: The time came near for God to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised Abraham. By then the number of our people in Egypt had grown larger and larger.
R.18: Then a new king began to rule Egypt. He did not know anything about Joseph.

decisions.choice: Exodus 1:7-8
decisions.reason: The people grew and multiplied (Exodus 1:7). The words of 7:18 follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 1:8 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: the time of the promise: the time for God to keep what he promised Abraham
alternatives: the time the promise was first made
decisions.reason: The promise is the one of 7:5-7, that Abraham's descendants would come out and worship God, and have the land.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "had declared"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "had sworn"; some early manuscripts have "had promised". The sense is close. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: did not know Joseph: knew nothing of him, or cared nothing for what he had done
decisions.reason: The new king had no regard for Joseph and what he had done for Egypt, and so none for his people (Exodus 1:9-10).

decisions.choice: the time came near for God to do what he had promised
alternatives: the time of the promise was drawing near
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the time of the promise" means, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: The people grow in Egypt, and Moses is born

records.source: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζῳογονεῖσθαι.
records.gloss: This one having dealt craftily with the race of us mistreated the fathers [of us] to make the infants exposed of them unto the not to be kept alive.
pieces: He schemed against our people and treated our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} cruelly. He made them put their babies out to die.

L.19: This one dealt craftily with our race and mistreated our fathers, making them expose their infants so that they would not be kept alive.

R.19: This king tricked our people and was cruel to them. He made our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} leave their babies outside so that they would die.

decisions.choice: Exodus 1:10-22
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 1:10 Pharaoh says "let us deal craftily with them", the same verb as here. He ordered the Hebrew boys to be killed (Exodus 1:16, 1:22).

decisions.choice: expose: leave a baby out in the open to die
decisions.reason: Leaving unwanted babies out to die was known in the ancient world. Exodus 1:22 has Pharaoh order every newborn boy thrown into the Nile.

decisions.choice: making them: Pharaoh forced the parents
alternatives: with the result that they exposed their babies
decisions.reason: The construction can express purpose or result. Either way, it was Pharaoh's cruelty that brought it about.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people of Israel in Egypt, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

records.source: ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·
records.gloss: In which time was born Moses, and was beautiful to the God; who was brought up months three in the house of the father.
pieces: That was the time when Moses was born, and he was a beautiful child before God. For three months he was cared for in his father's house.

L.20: At this time Moses was born, and he was beautiful to God. He was brought up three months in [his] father's house.

R.20: Moses was born at this time. God saw that he was a beautiful baby. For three months his parents took care of him at home.

decisions.choice: beautiful to God: beautiful in God's sight
alternatives: exceedingly beautiful, with "to God" as a way of saying "very"
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:2 says the child was fine; Hebrews 11:23 uses the same adjective. "To God" may mean in God's sight, or it may simply be an emphatic "very", as Jonah 3:3 calls Nineveh a city great "to God". Literal and Balanced keep both open; Readable follows the first.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:2: hidden for three months
decisions.reason: His mother hid him for three months before she could hide him no longer.

decisions.choice: his parents ... at home
decisions.reason: Readable says who cared for him; Exodus 2:2 speaks of his mother.

records.source: ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.
records.gloss: Having been put out then him took up him the daughter of Pharaoh and brought up him for herself as a son.
pieces: When he was put outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.

L.21: And when he was put out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up for herself as a son.

R.21: Then he was left outside. But Pharaoh's daughter took him home and raised him as her own son.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:3-10
decisions.reason: His mother put him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter found him, and he became her son (Exodus 2:10).

decisions.choice: took up: took him in as her own
decisions.reason: The verb was used of taking up a baby who had been exposed and adopting it, and "as a son" points the same way.

decisions.choice: put out: the same word as "expose" in 7:19
decisions.reason: Stephen uses the word of the king's cruel order. Exodus 2:3 shows Moses's mother placing him in a basket by the river.

records.source: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And was instructed Moses in all wisdom of Egyptians, was then mighty in words and deeds of him.
pieces: Moses was schooled in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he had power in what he said and in what he did.

L.22: And Moses was instructed in all [the] wisdom of [the] Egyptians, and he was mighty in his words and deeds.

R.22: Moses was taught everything the wise men of Egypt knew. He was a powerful man in the things he said and in the things he did.

decisions.choice: Moses's training and power: beyond what Exodus records
decisions.reason: Exodus does not tell of Moses's schooling, though as the son of Pharaoh's daughter he grew up at the court (Exodus 2:10). In Exodus 4:10 Moses says he is not a man of words. Stephen says he was mighty in words and deeds; the speech does not say how this fits with Exodus 4:10, and nothing is added to harmonize them.

decisions.choice: mighty in words and deeds: as Jesus was
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same words of Jesus (Luke 24:19).

decisions.choice: everything the wise men of Egypt knew
alternatives: all the wisdom of the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wisdom of Egypt was: the learning of its teachers.

records.source: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταετὴς χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.
records.gloss: When then was being fulfilled to him of forty years a time, it came up upon the heart of him to visit the brothers of him the sons of Israel.
pieces: As he reached the age of forty, he set his heart on visiting his own kin, the people of Israel.

L.23: And when a time of forty years was being fulfilled for him, it came up into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.

R.23: When Moses was about forty years old, he decided to go and see his own people, the Israelites. He wanted to see how they were doing.

decisions.choice: forty years old: Stephen's figure, not given in Exodus
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:11 says only "when Moses had grown up". Exodus 7:7 makes him eighty when he spoke to Pharaoh, and Deuteronomy 34:7 says he died at 120. Stephen's account divides Moses's life into three periods of forty years (7:23, 7:30, 7:36). The text does not say where the first figure comes from.

decisions.choice: it came up into his heart: he made up his mind
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying that a thought came to someone (Jeremiah 3:16; 1 Corinthians 2:9).

decisions.choice: visit: go to see, with care for them
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking after those in need (15:36; James 1:27), and of God visiting his people to help them (Luke 1:68).

decisions.choice: his own kin, the people of Israel; his own people, the Israelites
alternatives: his brothers, the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: "Brothers" and "sons of Israel" here mean his fellow Israelites, men and women; Balanced and Readable use inclusive words for them; Literal keeps the Greek ones.

decisions.choice: He wanted to see how they were doing
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the visit was out of care for them, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.
records.gloss: And having seen a certain one being wronged he defended [him] and did vengeance for the one being oppressed having struck the Egyptian.
pieces: Seeing one of them being wronged, he stepped in to defend him. He struck down the Egyptian and so avenged the man who was being abused.

L.24: And seeing one [of them] being wronged, he defended [him] and took vengeance for the one being oppressed, striking down the Egyptian.

R.24: He saw an Egyptian hurting one of the Israelites. So Moses helped the Israelite. He killed the Egyptian to pay him back for hurting the man.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:11-12
decisions.reason: Moses saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his kin, and killed the Egyptian.

decisions.choice: struck down: killed
decisions.reason: 7:28 says that Moses killed the Egyptian, as Exodus 2:12 does.

decisions.choice: an Egyptian hurting one of the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names who was wronged and by whom, as the end of the verse shows.

records.source: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.
records.gloss: He was supposing then to understand the brothers that the God through [the] hand of him is giving salvation to them; they but not understood.
pieces: He supposed his kin would grasp that God was bringing them salvation through his hand, but they did not grasp it.

L.25: And he supposed [his] brothers understood that God through his hand was giving them salvation, but they did not understand.

R.25: Moses thought his people would understand that God was using him to save them. But they did not understand.

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue from slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: Here the word means deliverance from oppression, as in the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 14:13. Stephen's hearers would also hear the word the apostles used of Jesus (4:12).

decisions.choice: through his hand: by means of him, as God's agent
decisions.reason: God is the one giving salvation; Moses is the one God works through (7:35).

decisions.choice: they did not understand: Israel failed to see whom God had sent
decisions.reason: This is Stephen's comment; Exodus does not say it. It fits the pattern of the speech: Joseph was rejected by his brothers (7:9), Moses by his people (7:35, 7:39), and Jesus by his (7:52). Peter speaks of the people acting in ignorance (3:17).

decisions.choice: his kin; his people
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means his fellow Israelites, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

records.source: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών· Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ἐστε· ἱνατί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;
records.gloss: On the and following day he appeared to them fighting and was reconciling them into peace having said, Men, brothers you are; why do you wrong one another?
pieces: On the following day he came upon some of them as they fought, and he tried to bring them back to peace: 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you wronging each other?'

L.26: And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them to peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers. Why do you wrong one another?'

R.26: The next day Moses saw two Israelites fighting. He tried to get them to stop and be at peace. He said, 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you hurting each other?'

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:13
decisions.reason: The next day Moses found two Hebrew men fighting and asked the one in the wrong why he was striking his fellow.

decisions.choice: was reconciling: tried to reconcile
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense here describes an attempt that did not succeed, as 7:27 shows.

decisions.choice: men, you are brothers: two men who belong to the same people
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:13 speaks of two Hebrew men. "Brothers" means fellow Israelites. No inclusive wording applies, since particular men are meant.

decisions.choice: two Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable says who was fighting, as Exodus 2:13 does.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφ’ ἡμῶν;
records.gloss: The one but wronging the neighbor pushed away him having said, Who you appointed ruler and judge over us?
pieces: But the one who was abusing his neighbor thrust Moses away and said, 'Who put you in charge as ruler and judge over us?

L.27: But the one wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?

R.27: But the man who was hurting the other man pushed Moses away. He said, 'Who made you our leader and judge?

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:14
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 2:14 word for word, and run on into 7:28.

decisions.choice: ruler: one with authority to lead and settle disputes
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 7:35, where God sends Moses as ruler.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses, since two other men are in view.

records.source: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;
records.gloss: Not to kill me you want the way you killed yesterday the Egyptian?
pieces: Do you mean to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'

L.28: You do not want to kill me in the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday, do you?'

R.28: Do you want to kill me too, the way you killed that Egyptian yesterday?'

decisions.choice: a scornful question
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect the answer no, but in this setting it is a taunt: the man knows what Moses did.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:14 continued
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 2:14. Moses then knew that the killing was known.

records.source: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.
records.gloss: Fled then Moses at the word this, and became a sojourner in [the] land of Midian, where he fathered sons two.
pieces: At these words Moses fled, and he lived as a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he had two sons.

L.29: And Moses fled at this word, and became a sojourner in [the] land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.

R.29: Because of what the man said, Moses ran away. He went to live in the land of Midian as a foreigner. There he had two sons.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:15-22 and 18:3-4
decisions.reason: Moses fled from Pharaoh to Midian, married Zipporah, and had two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living in a land not his own
decisions.reason: The same word as in 7:6, where Abraham's descendants live in a foreign land. Moses named his son Gershom, saying he had been a sojourner in a foreign land (Exodus 2:22).

decisions.choice: Midian: the land of the Midianites, in the desert lands south and east of Canaan
decisions.reason: The Midianites were a desert people descended from Abraham through Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2). The bounds of their land are not certain.

records.source: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου·
records.gloss: And having been fulfilled years forty appeared to him in the wilderness of the mountain Sinai an angel in a flame of fire of a bush.
pieces: When forty more years had gone by, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire within a bush.

L.30: And when forty years had been fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire of a bush.

R.30: Forty years went by. Then one day Moses was in the desert near Mount Sinai. An angel appeared to him there in the flames of a bush that was on fire.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:1-2, with the mountain called Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus 3:1 calls the mountain Horeb. The Old Testament uses both names for the mountain of God: Sinai in Exodus 19:11, Horeb in Deuteronomy 4:10 and 5:2.

decisions.choice: an angel: the angel of the Lord, through whom God himself spoke
alternatives: an angel acting on his own
decisions.reason: Exodus 3:2 says the angel of the LORD appeared in the flame, and then God speaks from the bush (3:4). Stephen too has the voice of the Lord speak (7:31).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "an angel"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "of the Lord", as in Exodus 3:2. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: forty years: the second forty years of Moses's life
decisions.reason: With 7:23 and 7:36, this divides Moses's 120 years (Deuteronomy 34:7) into three forties; Exodus 7:7 gives his age as eighty when he spoke to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: forty more years
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that these forty years follow the first forty of 7:23.

records.heading: The voice from the burning bush

records.source: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν τὸ ὅραμα.
records.gloss: The and Moses having seen marveled at the sight;
pieces: Moses was amazed when he saw this sight.

L.31: And when Moses saw [it], he marveled at the sight.

R.31: Moses was amazed at what he saw.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:3
decisions.reason: Moses turned aside to see why the bush was not burned up.

decisions.choice: the sight: something seen with the eyes
decisions.reason: The word is often used of visions (10:3, 16:9), but here it is the burning bush that Moses saw.

records.source: προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ κυρίου·
records.gloss: approaching then him to look came [the] voice of [the] Lord:
pieces: As he went closer to look, the voice of the Lord came to him:

L.31: And as he was coming near to look closely, there came [the] voice of [the] Lord:

R.31: He went closer to look at it. Then he heard the voice of the Lord, saying,

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:4: God calls from the bush
decisions.reason: When the LORD saw that Moses turned aside to look, God called to him from the bush.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew of Exodus 3
decisions.reason: The Greek has the word for Lord. In Exodus 3:4 the Hebrew has the divine name. The voice is God's own (7:32).

decisions.choice: came to him; saying
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add the words English needs to lead into the speech.

records.source: Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ.
records.gloss: I the God of the fathers of you, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
pieces: 'I am the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.'

L.32: 'I [am] the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.'

R.32: 'I am the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.'

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6
decisions.reason: God names himself as the God of Moses's fathers (Exodus 3:6, 3:15). Stephen gives these words before the command of Exodus 3:5 (7:33). Jesus quotes the same words in Luke 20:37.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means forebears, as in 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

records.source: ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.
records.gloss: Trembling then having become Moses not dared to look.
pieces: Moses was seized with trembling and did not dare to look.

L.32: And becoming terrified, Moses did not dare to look.

R.32: Moses was shaking with fear. He was too afraid to look.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6: Moses hid his face
decisions.reason: Exodus says Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου, ὁ γὰρ τόπος ἐφ’ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.
records.gloss: Said then to him the Lord, Loose the sandal of the feet of you, the for place on which you stand ground holy is.
pieces: The Lord said to him, 'Take the sandals off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.

L.33: Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.

R.33: The Lord said to him, 'Take off your sandals. The place where you are standing is holy ground.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:5
decisions.reason: The same command is given to Joshua (Joshua 5:15). In Exodus the Hebrew has the divine name in 3:4 and 3:7; the Greek here has "Lord".

decisions.choice: taking off the sandals: an act of reverence in a holy place
decisions.reason: Removing the sandals showed respect for God's presence (Joshua 5:15).

decisions.choice: holy ground, far from the land and the temple
decisions.reason: Stephen was charged with speaking against "the holy place" (6:13). Here a place in the desert outside the land is called holy, because God is present there.

records.source: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα, καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς· καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
records.gloss: Having seen I saw the mistreatment of the people of me the in Egypt, and the groaning of them I heard, and I came down to rescue them; and now come, I will send you into Egypt.
pieces: I have seen, yes, seen the cruelty done to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt. I have heard them groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Come now: I will send you to Egypt.'

L.34: I have surely seen the mistreatment of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. And now come, I will send you to Egypt.'

R.34: I have seen how badly {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are being treated in Egypt. I have heard them crying out. I have come down to rescue them. So come now. I am sending you to Egypt.'

decisions.choice: seeing I saw: I have surely seen
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of stressing a verb, carried into the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 3:7.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:7-8 and 3:10
decisions.reason: God has seen his people's suffering, heard their cry, and come down to deliver them, and he sends Moses to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: I have come down: God acts in the world
decisions.reason: The Old Testament speaks of God coming down to see or to act (Genesis 11:5, 18:21).

decisions.choice: I have seen, yes, seen
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress of the doubled verb by repeating it.

records.source: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν, ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν, τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ.
records.gloss: This the Moses, whom they denied having said, Who you appointed ruler and judge? this one the God both ruler and redeemer has sent with [the] hand of [the] angel the having appeared to him in the bush.
pieces: This was the Moses they had pushed away with the words 'Who made you ruler and judge?' God sent this very man to be both ruler and redeemer, with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.

L.35: This Moses, whom they disowned, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?', this one God has sent as both ruler and redeemer, with [the] hand of [the] angel who appeared to him in the bush.

R.35: The Israelites had turned away from Moses. They had said to him, 'Who made you our leader and judge?' But God sent this same Moses to be their leader and to set them free. God sent him with the help of the angel that Moses saw in the bush.

decisions.choice: disowned: refused to accept him
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 3:13-14 of the people disowning Jesus before Pilate.

decisions.choice: the one they rejected is the one God sent
decisions.reason: "This Moses ... this one" is repeated through 7:35-38. Peter spoke the same way of Jesus: the one they rejected God made Lord and Messiah (2:36, 4:11). The speech does not draw the line in so many words until 7:52.

decisions.choice: redeemer: one who sets free
decisions.reason: In Exodus 6:6 God says he will redeem Israel from Egypt. The disciples on the road to Emmaus had hoped Jesus would redeem Israel (Luke 24:21).

decisions.choice: with the hand of the angel: with the angel's help
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means help or agency.

decisions.choice: to be their leader and to set them free
decisions.reason: Readable says what "ruler" and "redeemer" mean here.

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names those who turned Moses away.

records.source: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.
records.gloss: This one led out them having done wonders and signs in [the] land of Egypt and in [the] Red Sea and in the wilderness years forty.
pieces: It was he who brought them out, working wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.

L.36: This one led them out, doing wonders and signs in [the] land of Egypt and at [the] Red Sea and in the wilderness forty years.

R.36: Moses led the people out of Egypt. He did wonders and signs to show God's power. He did them in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and during the forty years in the desert.

decisions.choice: the plagues, the crossing of the sea, and the years in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Exodus 7-14 tells of the signs in Egypt and at the sea; Numbers 14:33-34 of the forty years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: wonders and signs: acts of power that show God at work
decisions.reason: The same pair is used of Jesus (2:22), of the apostles (2:43, 5:12), and of Stephen himself (6:8).

decisions.choice: the Red Sea: the name the Greek Old Testament gives the sea Israel crossed
alternatives: the sea now called the Red Sea, with certainty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls it the Sea of Reeds (Exodus 13:18, 15:4). Just which body of water it was is not certain.

decisions.choice: to show God's power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wonders and signs were for, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ.
records.gloss: This is the Moses the having said to the sons of Israel, A prophet for you will raise up the God out from the brothers of you like me.
pieces: This is the Moses who told the people of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people.'

L.37: This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet from your brothers, like me.'

R.37: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, 'God will send you a prophet like me. He will come from your own people.'

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 18:15: the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: Peter quoted the same promise of Jesus (3:22).

decisions.choice: the prophet like Moses is Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter applies the promise to Jesus (3:22-26). Stephen sets it here, between Moses rejected and the people's idolatry.

decisions.choice: your brothers: your own people, Israel
decisions.reason: The prophet would be an Israelite, as in 3:22.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "like me"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "him you shall hear", from Deuteronomy 18:15. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel, the Israelites; your own people
alternatives: the sons of Israel; your brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrases mean, as in 3:22; Literal keeps the Greek words.

records.source: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐδέξατο λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ἡμῖν, ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον, εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών· Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν· ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: This is the one having been in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel the speaking to him in the mountain Sinai and the fathers of us, who received oracles living to give to us, \v 39 to whom not were willing obedient to become the fathers of us, but pushed away and turned in the hearts of them to Egypt, \v 40 having said to the Aaron, Make for us gods who will go before us; the for Moses this, who led out us from [the] land of Egypt, not we know what happened to him.
pieces: He was there in the assembly in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai and with our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, and he received living words to pass on to us.
Yet our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} would not submit to him. They thrust him aside, and their hearts went back to Egypt.
'Make us gods to lead the way for us,' they told Aaron. 'This Moses who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him.'

L.38: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; he received living oracles to give to us.
L.39: Our fathers were not willing to become obedient to him, but they pushed [him] away and turned back in their hearts to Egypt,
L.40: saying to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will go before us; for this Moses who led us out of [the] land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'

R.38: Moses was with the assembly of God's people in the desert. The angel spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and Moses was there with our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. Moses received words from God that give life, and he passed them on to us.
R.39: But our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} would not obey Moses. They turned away from him. In their hearts they wanted to go back to Egypt.
R.40: They said to Aaron, 'Make us gods to lead us. This Moses brought us out of Egypt, but we do not know what has happened to him.'

decisions.choice: assembly: Israel gathered as God's people in the wilderness
alternatives: the church of believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the church (5:11), but here it means Israel gathered before God at Sinai. The Greek Old Testament uses it for "the day of the assembly" when the law was given (Deuteronomy 4:10, 9:10, 18:16).

decisions.choice: the angel who spoke at Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus tells of God speaking to Moses on the mountain. Other passages speak of angels at the giving of the law: Deuteronomy 33:2 in the Greek Old Testament, Galatians 3:19, Hebrews 2:2, and Stephen himself in 7:53.

decisions.choice: living oracles: words from God that are alive and give life
alternatives: oracles that are still in force
decisions.reason: "Oracles" are words spoken by God (Romans 3:2). The law gave life to those who kept it (Leviticus 18:5; Deuteronomy 32:47).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to give to us"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "to you". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Numbers 14:3-4 and Exodus 32:1, 32:23
decisions.reason: The people wanted to go back to Egypt (Numbers 14:3-4). Their words to Aaron follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 32:1 and 32:23 closely.

decisions.choice: turned back in their hearts to Egypt: longed to return to Egypt
decisions.reason: They did not go back, but they wanted to (Numbers 11:5, 14:3).

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people of Israel in the wilderness, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: living words; words from God that give life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plainer words for "oracles", as the meaning note explains.

records.source: καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ, καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And they made a calf in the days those and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of the hands of them.
pieces: Then it was that they fashioned a calf. They offered a sacrifice to the idol and held a celebration over the work of their hands.

L.41: And they made a calf in those days, and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and they were rejoicing in the works of their hands.

R.41: At that time they made a statue of a calf. They offered a sacrifice to this idol. They had a big party to celebrate the thing they had made with their own hands.

decisions.choice: Exodus 32:4-6: the golden calf
decisions.reason: Aaron made a calf of gold; the people offered sacrifices, ate and drank, and rose up to play.

decisions.choice: made a calf: made an image of a young bull
decisions.reason: One Greek verb says "made a calf". It was an image cast in gold (Exodus 32:4).

decisions.choice: the works of their hands: idols they had made
decisions.reason: The Old Testament scorns idols as the work of human hands (Deuteronomy 4:28; Psalm 115:4). Compare 7:48.

decisions.choice: were rejoicing: kept on celebrating
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures the feasting going on.

records.source: ἔστρεψεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν· Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ;
records.gloss: Turned then the God and handed over them to worship the host of the heaven, as it has been written in [the] book of the prophets, Not slain beasts and sacrifices did you offer to me years forty in the wilderness, house of Israel?
pieces: So God turned away and gave them over to worship the stars of the sky, as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} slaughtered animals and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?

L.42: But God turned and handed them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in [the] book of the prophets: 'You did not offer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} slain beasts and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, did you, house of Israel?

R.42: But God turned away from them. He let them go on worshiping the sun, moon and stars. This is what is written in the book of the prophets: 'People of Israel, you did not bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} animals to kill and offer as sacrifices during those forty years in the desert, did you?

decisions.choice: God turned and handed them over: he let them go the way they chose
alternatives: God caused them to worship the stars
decisions.reason: God's judgment is to give people over to what they have chosen, as in Romans 1:24, 1:26 and 1:28.

decisions.choice: the host of heaven: the sun, moon and stars, worshiped as gods
decisions.reason: The law forbade worshiping the host of heaven (Deuteronomy 4:19, 17:3); Israel and Judah did so later (2 Kings 17:16, 21:3; Jeremiah 8:2).

decisions.choice: the book of the prophets: the twelve shorter prophetic books, kept as one scroll
decisions.reason: The words come from Amos, one of the twelve. These books were copied together as one book.

decisions.choice: Amos 5:25-27 in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Stephen quotes Amos 5:25-27 in the form of the Greek Old Testament, which differs from the Hebrew in 5:26-27 (see 7:43).

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect "no". It may mean that Israel did not offer sacrifices to God in the wilderness at all, or that what they offered was not truly offered to him. Every level keeps the question open between these two.

decisions.choice: the stars of the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the host of heaven is, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: Readable names what was worshiped.

records.source: καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ Ῥαιφάν, τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: and you took up the tent of the Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images which you made to worship them;
pieces: You lifted up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images you made in order to bow down to them.

L.43: And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images that you made in order to worship them.

R.43: You carried the tent of the god Moloch. You carried the star of the god Rephan. You made these images so that you could worship them.

decisions.choice: Amos 5:26 in the Greek Old Testament, which differs from the Hebrew
decisions.reason: Stephen follows the Greek Old Testament of Amos 5:26, which reads "the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Raiphan". The Hebrew text has different words: "Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god". The meaning of Sikkuth and Kiyyun is uncertain; they may be names of gods linked with the stars. The speech does not discuss the difference.

decisions.choice: the tent of Moloch: a portable shrine of the god Moloch
decisions.reason: Moloch was a god to whom children were sacrificed, which the law forbade (Leviticus 18:21, 20:2-5; 2 Kings 23:10). The tent stands against the tent of the testimony in 7:44.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the god Rephan"
decisions.reason: The name is spelled in several ways in the manuscripts (Rephan, Remphan, Raiphan and others), and many manuscripts add "your" before "god". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: images: figures shaped by hand
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 7:44 for the pattern of the tabernacle: Israel made images of its own, instead of what God had shown.

decisions.choice: bow down to
decisions.reason: The verb pictures bowing down in worship; Balanced uses that picture.

records.source: καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος.
records.gloss: and I will remove you beyond Babylon.
pieces: So I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.'

L.43: And I will deport you beyond Babylon.'

R.43: So I will take you away from your land and send you far beyond Babylon.'

decisions.choice: beyond Babylon: Amos has "beyond Damascus"
alternatives: the text of Amos as it stands
decisions.reason: Amos 5:27, in both the Hebrew and the Greek Old Testament, says "beyond Damascus". Amos spoke to the northern kingdom of Israel, which Assyria took into exile (2 Kings 17:6). Babylon was where Judah was later taken (2 Kings 24-25). The speech gives the place as Babylon and does not say why it differs from Amos; nothing is added to explain it.

decisions.choice: remove: deport, resettle by force
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:4, where God moved Abraham into the land. Now God will move the people out of it.

decisions.choice: from your land
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deporting means.

records.source: Ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἦν τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθὼς διετάξατο ὁ λαλῶν τῷ Μωϋσῇ ποιῆσαι αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸν τύπον ὃν ἑωράκει, ἣν καὶ εἰσήγαγον διαδεξάμενοι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν ἐξῶσεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἕως τῶν ἡμερῶν Δαυίδ·
records.gloss: The tent of the testimony was to the fathers of us in the wilderness, as commanded the one speaking to the Moses to make it according to the pattern which he had seen, \v 45 which also brought in having received in turn the fathers of us with Joshua in the possession of the nations, whom drove out the God from [the] face of the fathers of us, until the days of David,
pieces: In the wilderness our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had the tent of the testimony, made as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who spoke to Moses had directed, following the pattern Moses had seen.

Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} received it in their turn and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the lands of the nations, whom God drove out ahead of them. So it was until the days of David.

L.44: Our fathers had the tent of the testimony in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses commanded [him] to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
L.45: Our fathers in turn, having received it, also brought it in with Joshua when they took possession [of the land] of the nations, whom God drove out before our fathers, until the days of David.

R.44: Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had the holy tent with them in the desert. It was called the tent of the testimony. God had told Moses to make it just like the plan that Moses had been shown.
R.45: Later the next generation of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} received the tent. They brought it with them when they went with Joshua into the land. God forced out the nations who lived there as our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} came in. Things stayed that way until the time of David.

decisions.choice: the tent of the testimony: the tabernacle, the tent where God met Israel
decisions.reason: It held the ark with the tablets of the testimony, the covenant law (Exodus 25:16, 25:21, 38:21; Numbers 1:50). It stands against the tent of Moloch in 7:43.

decisions.choice: Exodus 25:9 and 25:40: made by the pattern shown on the mountain
decisions.reason: God told Moses to make the tabernacle by the pattern he was shown on the mountain. Hebrews 8:5 quotes Exodus 25:40.

decisions.choice: Joshua: Joshua son of Nun
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the name Joshua is the same as the name Jesus. Here it is Joshua, who led Israel into the land with the tabernacle (Joshua 3:14-17, 18:1).

decisions.choice: until the days of David: the time the tent remained, with the driving out of the nations
alternatives: the driving out of the nations alone
decisions.reason: The phrase may tell how long God went on driving out the nations, or how long things stayed as they were, with the tent and no temple. Literal keeps both open; Balanced and Readable take it of the whole situation, leading into 7:46.

decisions.choice: received in turn: took it over from those before them
decisions.reason: The tent was handed down from the generation of the wilderness to the next.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people of Israel in earlier generations, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: the holy tent; the next generation
alternatives: the tent; having received in turn
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of tent it was and who received it.

records.heading: The tent in the wilderness and the house Solomon built

records.source: ὃς εὗρεν χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ᾐτήσατο εὑρεῖν σκήνωμα τῷ θεῷ Ἰακώβ.
records.gloss: who found favor before the God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
pieces: God looked on David with favor, and David asked to be allowed to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

L.46: He found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

R.46: God was pleased with David. David asked God to let him make a home for the God of Jacob.

decisions.choice: favor: God's goodwill toward David
decisions.reason: The word is the one often translated grace, but the phrase "found favor before God" is an Old Testament way of saying that God was pleased with someone (Genesis 6:8; Luke 1:30).

decisions.choice: Psalm 132:2-5 and 2 Samuel 7:1-2
decisions.reason: David vowed to find a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob (Psalm 132:5), and wished to build a house for the ark (2 Samuel 7:2).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "for the God of Jacob"
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts read "for the house of Jacob"; others, with many later ones, read "for the God of Jacob", as in Psalm 132:5. The two Greek words differ by only a few letters. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: dwelling place: a dwelling, a word related to "tent"
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for tent in 7:44. David asked for a dwelling; 7:47 says Solomon built a house.

decisions.choice: David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David, from the end of 7:45.

decisions.choice: make a home
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for "find a dwelling place".

records.source: Σολομῶν δὲ οἰκοδόμησεν αὐτῷ οἶκον.
records.gloss: Solomon however built for him a house.
pieces: But it was Solomon who built a house for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.47: But Solomon built a house for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.47: But it was Solomon, David's son, who built a house for God.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 6 and 8: Solomon builds the temple
decisions.reason: God told David that his son would build the house (2 Samuel 7:12-13; 1 Kings 8:17-20).

decisions.choice: a house: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The temple is called the house of God (Luke 19:46).

decisions.choice: but: a contrast with David's dwelling, without a judgment on Solomon
alternatives: a criticism of Solomon for building
decisions.reason: The small word marks a contrast between David's request and Solomon's house. Whether it carries blame is not said; 7:48 makes the point that God does not live in houses made by hands.

decisions.choice: David's son; God
decisions.reason: Readable says who Solomon was and names God.

records.source: ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὁ ὕψιστος ἐν χειροποιήτοις κατοικεῖ· καθὼς ὁ προφήτης λέγει·
records.gloss: But not the Most High in hand-made dwells, as the prophet says,
pieces: Yet the Most High does not make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home in buildings that hands have made, as the prophet says:

L.48: But the Most High does not dwell in [houses] made by hands, as the prophet says:

R.48: But the Most High God does not live in buildings that people make. Here is what God said through the prophet:

decisions.choice: made by hands: made by human beings
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament the word is used for idols (Leviticus 26:1; Isaiah 2:18). Jesus was accused of speaking of a temple made with hands (Mark 14:58), and Paul says God does not live in such temples (17:24).

decisions.choice: Solomon's own words at the temple
decisions.reason: At the dedication Solomon said that heaven itself cannot contain God, much less the house he had built (1 Kings 8:27).

decisions.choice: the Most High: a title of God
decisions.reason: Used of God in Genesis 14:18-20 and in Luke 1:32, 1:35.

decisions.choice: Here is what God said through the prophet
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the words that follow are God's, as 7:49 says.

records.source: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου· ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, λέγει κύριος, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου;
records.gloss: The heaven to me a throne, the and earth a footstool of the feet of me; what kind of house will you build for me, says [the] Lord, or what [is the] place of the rest of me?
pieces: 'Heaven is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, and the earth is the footstool under {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. What sort of house could you build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says the Lord, or what place could be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} resting place?

L.49: 'Heaven [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, and the earth a footstool for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. What kind of house will you build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says [the] Lord, or what [is the] place of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest?

R.49: 'Heaven is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne. The earth is where I rest {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. So what kind of house could you build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says the Lord. What place could you make for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to rest in?

decisions.choice: Isaiah 66:1 in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Stephen quotes Isaiah 66:1-2. The Greek has "Lord"; the Hebrew of Isaiah 66:1 has the divine name.

decisions.choice: a footstool for my feet: the earth is small beside God's throne
alternatives: the earth is under God's feet as a conquered enemy
decisions.reason: Heaven is God's throne and the whole earth only the place for his feet. No house on earth could hold him.

decisions.choice: the place of my rest: a place for God to dwell
decisions.reason: God's resting place is his dwelling (Psalm 132:8, 132:14), the place David sought to find (7:46).

records.source: οὐχὶ ἡ χείρ μου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα πάντα;
records.gloss: Not the hand of me made these things all?
pieces: Was it not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand that made all these things?'

L.50: Did not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand make all these things?'

R.50: Did I not make all these things with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own hand?'

decisions.choice: Isaiah 66:2, as a question
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the words are a statement: all these things my hand has made. Here they are a question expecting yes.

decisions.choice: God made all things, so no house can contain him
decisions.reason: "All these things" are heaven and earth. Paul makes the same point in Athens (17:24).

records.source: Σκληροτράχηλοι καὶ ἀπερίτμητοι καρδίαις καὶ τοῖς ὠσίν, ὑμεῖς ἀεὶ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε, ὡς οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ὑμεῖς.
records.gloss: Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and in the ears, you always the Spirit the Holy resist, as the fathers of you also you.
pieces: How stubborn you are! Your hearts and ears are uncircumcised. You are forever fighting against the Holy Spirit, and you do what your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} did.

L.51: Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers [did], you also [do].

R.51: You are so stubborn! Your hearts are closed to God, and your ears will not listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You always fight against the Holy Spirit, just as your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} did.

decisions.choice: stiff-necked: stubborn, refusing to obey
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that will not bend its neck to the yoke. God calls Israel stiff-necked after the golden calf (Exodus 32:9, 33:3, 33:5).

decisions.choice: uncircumcised in hearts and ears: closed to God within, though marked as his people outwardly
decisions.reason: The prophets and the law speak of hearts and ears that are uncircumcised, unwilling to hear and obey (Leviticus 26:41; Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4, 6:10). The charge stands against the covenant of circumcision in 7:8.

decisions.choice: resisting the Holy Spirit, as Israel did in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Isaiah 63:10 says they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forebears of the people, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: Your hearts are closed to God, and your ears will not listen to him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: Which of the prophets not persecuted the fathers of you?
pieces: Which one of the prophets escaped persecution by your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}?

L.52: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute?

R.52: Your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} made trouble for every one of the prophets!

decisions.choice: the persecution of the prophets
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 36:16 and Nehemiah 9:26 tell how Israel mocked and killed God's prophets; Jesus said the same (Luke 11:47-51, 13:34).

decisions.choice: a question that means: they persecuted every one
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "none".

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
alternatives: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute?
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the question means.

records.source: καὶ ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ δικαίου οὗ νῦν ὑμεῖς προδόται καὶ φονεῖς ἐγένεσθε, οἵτινες ἐλάβετε τὸν νόμον εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξατε.
records.gloss: And they killed those having announced beforehand about the coming of the Righteous One, of whom now you betrayers and murderers have become, \v 53 who received the law as ordinances of angels and not kept [it].
pieces: They killed those who told in advance of the coming of the Righteous One, and you have now become {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} betrayers and murderers.
The law was given to you through angels, but you have not kept it."

L.52: And they killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers,
L.53: you who received the law as ordinances of angels and did not keep [it]."

R.52: They killed the prophets who said long ago that the Righteous One would come. And now you have betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and murdered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.53: You received God's law, and angels brought it to you. But you have not obeyed it."
