decisions.choice: the Righteous One: a title for Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter calls Jesus the Holy and Righteous One (3:14), and Ananias calls him the Righteous One (22:14). Isaiah 53:11 speaks of the righteous servant.

decisions.choice: betrayers and murderers: they handed him over and had him killed
alternatives: they killed him with their own hands
decisions.reason: The council handed Jesus over to Pilate and called for his death (Luke 23:1-25; Acts 3:13-15). Stephen now turns from "your fathers" to "you".

decisions.choice: as ordinances of angels: delivered through angels
decisions.reason: The law came from God through angels (Galatians 3:19; Hebrews 2:2; Deuteronomy 33:2 in the Greek Old Testament), as in 7:38.

decisions.choice: you did not keep the law
decisions.reason: Stephen was charged with speaking against the law (6:13). He ends by charging his accusers with not keeping it.

decisions.choice: you have now become his betrayers and murderers; you have betrayed him and murdered him
alternatives: of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the relative clause into a main clause.

decisions.choice: the prophets; God's law
decisions.reason: Readable says who was killed and whose law it was.

records.source: Ἀκούοντες δὲ ταῦτα διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Hearing then these things they were cut in the hearts of them and were gnashing the teeth at him.
pieces: Hearing these words, they seethed with fury and ground their teeth at Stephen.

L.54: And hearing these things, they were cut to their hearts and were gnashing their teeth at him.

R.54: The council members became very angry when they heard this. They were so angry that they ground their teeth at Stephen.

decisions.choice: cut to their hearts: furious
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 5:33, when the council wanted to kill the apostles. It is not the word for being stung to repentance in 2:37.

decisions.choice: gnashing their teeth: showing rage
decisions.reason: The Psalms picture the wicked gnashing their teeth at the righteous (Psalm 35:16, 37:12).

decisions.choice: Stephen; the council members
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Stephen, and Readable names the council.

records.heading: Stephen sees the Son of Man, and is stoned

records.source: ὑπάρχων δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶδεν δόξαν θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς διηνοιγμένους καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Being but full of [the] Spirit Holy, having looked intently into the heaven he saw [the] glory of God and Jesus standing at [the] right of the God, \v 56 and said, Behold, I see the heavens having been opened and the Son of the Man at [the] right standing of the God.
pieces: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Stephen fixed his gaze on heaven. He saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at God's right hand.
He said, "Look! I see the heavens opened wide, and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand."

L.55: But being full of [the] Holy Spirit, he looked intently into heaven and saw [the] glory of God, and Jesus standing at [the] right [hand] of God,
L.56: and he said, "Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at [the] right [hand] of God."

R.55: But Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit. He looked up into heaven and saw the glory of God. He saw Jesus standing at God's right side, in the place of honor.
R.56: Stephen said, "Look! I see heaven open. I see the Son of Man standing at God's right side."

decisions.choice: standing: Jesus stands at God's right hand
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jesus is seated at God's right hand (Luke 22:69; Psalm 110:1). Here he is standing. It may picture him rising to receive Stephen, or standing as a witness for him, or it may simply describe him there. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: the right hand of God: the place of honor and power
decisions.reason: Peter said Jesus was exalted to God's right hand (2:33-34).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's own title for himself
decisions.reason: Jesus used it of himself, and before the council he said that the Son of Man would be seated at the right hand of God (Luke 22:69; Daniel 7:13-14). This is the only time in Acts the title is used, and here it is spoken by Stephen, not by Jesus.

decisions.choice: the glory of God: as at the start of the speech
decisions.reason: The speech began with "the God of glory" appearing to Abraham (7:2), and ends with Stephen seeing God's glory.

decisions.choice: opened: opened, and standing open
decisions.reason: The perfect tense shows heaven opened and remaining open (compare Luke 3:21).

decisions.choice: Stephen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Stephen.

decisions.choice: in the place of honor
alternatives: at the right hand of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the right hand of God means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν, καὶ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν.
records.gloss: Having cried out then in voice loud they held together the ears of them and rushed with one accord upon him, \v 58 and having cast [him] out of the city they were stoning [him].
pieces: They let out a great shout, covered their ears, and rushed at him all together.
They drove him out of the city and began to stone him.

L.57: But crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed with one accord at him,
L.58: and casting [him] out of the city, they began stoning [him].

R.57: Then they all shouted loudly and covered their ears. Together they rushed at Stephen.
R.58: They threw him out of the city and began to throw stones at him to kill him.

decisions.choice: stopped their ears: refused to hear what they took as blasphemy
decisions.reason: Covering the ears shut out words they judged an offense against God.

decisions.choice: stoning outside the city
decisions.reason: The law gave stoning as the penalty for blasphemy, and it was carried out outside the camp or the town (Leviticus 24:14-16; Numbers 15:35-36; Deuteronomy 17:5-7). The text does not say whether the council passed a sentence or the crowd acted on its own. Under Roman rule the council was not permitted to put anyone to death (John 18:31).

decisions.choice: were stoning: began stoning, and went on
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures the stoning going on, as in 7:59.

decisions.choice: throw stones at him to kill him
decisions.reason: Readable says what stoning was.

records.source: καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας νεανίου καλουμένου Σαύλου.
records.gloss: And the witnesses laid aside the garments of them at the feet of a young man being called Saul.
pieces: The witnesses put their cloaks down at the feet of a young man named Saul.

L.58: And the witnesses laid aside their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.

R.58: The men who had spoken against Stephen took off their coats. They left them with a young man named Saul.

decisions.choice: the witnesses: those who testified, who threw the first stones
decisions.reason: The law required the witnesses to be the first to put the condemned to death (Deuteronomy 17:7). These are the false witnesses of 6:13.

decisions.choice: a young man: a man in the early part of adult life
decisions.reason: The word does not give an exact age.

decisions.choice: Saul: the first mention of the man later called Paul
decisions.reason: He approved of the killing (8:1), and later recalled guarding the garments of those who killed Stephen (22:20). He is called Paul from 13:9.

decisions.choice: the men who had spoken against Stephen
decisions.reason: Readable says who the witnesses were, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: καὶ ἐλιθοβόλουν τὸν Στέφανον ἐπικαλούμενον καὶ λέγοντα· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου·
records.gloss: And they were stoning the Stephen calling upon and saying, Lord Jesus, receive the spirit of me.
pieces: As they stoned Stephen, he called out, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

L.59: And they were stoning Stephen as he called out and said, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

R.59: While they were throwing stones at Stephen, he prayed. He said, "Lord Jesus, take my spirit to be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: calling out: calling on the Lord in prayer
decisions.reason: The verb is used of calling on the name of the Lord (2:21, 22:16). Stephen prays to Jesus.

decisions.choice: receive my spirit: as Jesus prayed on the cross
decisions.reason: Jesus committed his spirit to the Father (Luke 23:46), in the words of Psalm 31:6. Stephen commits his spirit to Jesus.

decisions.choice: take my spirit to be with you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "receive" means here.

records.source: θεὶς δὲ τὰ γόνατα ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Κύριε, μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν· καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐκοιμήθη.
records.gloss: Having placed then the knees he cried out in voice loud, Lord, not set to them this the sin. And this having said he fell asleep.
pieces: Then he sank to his knees and cried out in a loud voice, "Lord, do not charge them with this sin." With these words he fell asleep.

L.60: And falling on [his] knees, he cried out with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." And having said this, he fell asleep.

R.60: Then he got down on his knees and shouted, "Lord, do not blame them for this sin!" After he said this, he died.

decisions.choice: do not set this sin to them: do not count it against them
decisions.reason: Stephen asks the Lord not to hold the sin to their account.

decisions.choice: as Jesus prayed for those who crucified him
decisions.reason: Jesus prayed, "Father, forgive them" (Luke 23:34). That verse is missing from some early manuscripts of Luke.

decisions.choice: fell asleep: died
decisions.reason: Death is spoken of as sleep, especially the death of God's people (13:36; John 11:11-14; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14).

decisions.choice: he died
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "fell asleep" means here, as the meaning note explains.
